name: VMware ESXi
tagline: Bare-metal ESXi hosting a private domain, NAT gateway and remote desktops.

howItWorks.title: Hypervisor (L1)
howItWorks.body:
ESXi boots from a small device and runs the VMkernel directly on the hardware.
Physical NICs (vmnic) are the only L1 link to the outside.
Datastores hold each VM as a folder of .vmx and .vmdk files.

howItWorks.title: vSwitches (L2)
howItWorks.body:
A standard vSwitch is a software switch; uplinks are the vmnics attached to it.
A vSwitch with no uplink is a private network for VMs on that host only.
Port groups set the VLAN ID and security policy per VM network.

howItWorks.title: Gateway VM (L3)
howItWorks.body:
One NIC sits on the public vSwitch, the other on the private vSwitch.
IP forwarding and a MASQUERADE rule NAT private hosts to the WAN address.
Port forwards (DNAT) publish 443 to the RD Gateway.

howItWorks.title: Active Directory services
howItWorks.body:
DC01 runs AD DS, DNS and DHCP for the private subnet.
Clients get the DHCP scope, DNS suffix and the gateway VM as default route.
DC02 joins as a second DC and can take over all five FSMO roles.

howItWorks.title: Remote desktops (L7)
howItWorks.body:
RD Gateway wraps RDP in HTTPS on 443 with a certificate.
The Connection Broker sends users to a session host in the collection.
File shares live on a file server reached over SMB.
A jumpbox is the single admin entry for RDP and SSH.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
Users: remote desktop clients and administrators on the physical network.
Edge: a firewall or the gateway VM receives HTTPS, then NATs it to the private side.
Uplinks trunk VLANs to the physical switch; port groups tag each VM network.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Platform services: Windows Server roles, Linux VMs or a Kubernetes cluster on VMs.
Infrastructure: datastores on local disk, NFS, iSCSI or vSAN hold the VM files.
The vSphere CSI driver provisions Kubernetes volumes on datastores.
vCenter manages many hosts; vMotion and vSphere HA need shared storage and a common network.

howItWorks.title: Operators and automation
howItWorks.body:
Operators use the Host Client, vCenter, SSH (only when needed) or esxcli.
Terraform's vSphere provider, Ansible's VMware collection and govc automate the VM lifecycle.
Snapshots are short-term; use a backup product for restores.
esxtop and vCenter charts show CPU ready, memory ballooning and datastore latency.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
Hypervisor: KVM or Proxmox on Linux, Microsoft Hyper-V, Xen. Choose KVM or Proxmox to avoid licence cost.
Cloud-style IaaS on KVM: OpenStack. Public cloud: AWS EC2, Azure VMs.
Gateway and firewall: pfSense, OPNsense, VyOS or a Linux VM with iptables.
Directory: Samba AD, FreeIPA or Entra ID instead of Windows AD.

flow: A user connects to the RD Gateway name over HTTPS on 443.
The frame enters vSwitch0 through the physical uplink.
The gateway VM forwards 443 to the RD Gateway with DNAT.
RD Gateway authenticates against AD DS and checks its policies.
The Connection Broker picks a session host from the collection.
The session host maps file shares from the file server over SMB.
Return traffic leaves through the gateway VM, translated by NAT.

deploy.summary: On-prem bring-up on a single host: network first, then domain, then desktops and migration.
prerequisites: A server on the ESXi 8.0 hardware compatibility list
Windows Server 2022 ISO and a Linux ISO for the gateway
A workstation with an SSH key pair

steps.title: 1. Static management address, DNS and hostname
steps.code:
esxcli network ip interface ipv4 set -i vmk0 -t static -I 192.168.1.10 -N 255.255.255.0
esxcli network ip route ipv4 add --network default --gateway 192.168.1.1
esxcli network ip dns server add --server 192.168.1.1
esxcli system hostname set --host esx01 --domain lab.local
steps.note: Run in the console shell after install. Placeholders match your WAN subnet.

steps.title: 2. SSH with keys, scoped by firewall
steps.code:
vim-cmd hostsvc/enable_ssh && vim-cmd hostsvc/start_ssh
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f ~/.ssh/esx01
ssh-copy-id -f -i ~/.ssh/esx01.pub root@192.168.1.10
esxcli network firewall ruleset set --ruleset-id sshServer --allowed-all false
esxcli network firewall ruleset allowedip add --ruleset-id sshServer --ip-address 192.168.1.0/24
ssh -i ~/.ssh/esx01 root@192.168.1.10
steps.note: If ssh-copy-id fails, append the key to /etc/ssh/keys-root/authorized_keys. Run vim-cmd hostsvc/stop_ssh when done.

steps.title: 3. Private vSwitch1 with no uplink
steps.code:
esxcli network vswitch standard add -v vSwitch1
esxcli network vswitch standard portgroup add -v vSwitch1 -p LAN-Private
esxcli network vswitch standard policy security set -v vSwitch1 --allow-promiscuous=false --allow-forged-transmits=false --allow-mac-change=false
esxcli network vswitch standard list
steps.note: vSwitch1 has no vmnic, so frames never leave the host. vSwitch0 keeps vmnic0.

steps.title: 4. Gateway VM: two NICs, forwarding and NAT
steps.code:
# eth0 = WAN on vSwitch0 (192.168.1.5), eth1 = LAN on vSwitch1
sudo ip addr add 192.168.10.1/24 dev eth1 && sudo ip link set eth1 up
echo 'net.ipv4.ip_forward=1' | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-forward.conf && sudo sysctl --system
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -s 192.168.10.0/24 -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -i eth1 -o eth0 -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -i eth0 -o eth1 -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i eth0 -p tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.168.10.20:443
steps.note: Persist the addresses in netplan or NetworkManager and the rules with iptables-persistent. 192.168.10.20 is the RD Gateway.

steps.title: 5. DC01: AD DS, DNS and DHCP
steps.code:
New-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias Ethernet0 -IPAddress 192.168.10.10 -PrefixLength 24 -DefaultGateway 192.168.10.1
Rename-Computer DC01 -Restart
Install-WindowsFeature AD-Domain-Services,DNS,DHCP -IncludeManagementTools
Install-ADDSForest -DomainName lab.local -DomainNetbiosName LAB -InstallDns
Add-DhcpServerInDC -DnsName dc01.lab.local
Add-DhcpServerv4Scope -Name LAN -StartRange 192.168.10.100 -EndRange 192.168.10.200 -SubnetMask 255.255.255.0
Set-DhcpServerv4OptionValue -ScopeId 192.168.10.0 -Router 192.168.10.1 -DnsServer 192.168.10.10 -DnsDomain lab.local
steps.note: Run in two stages around the restart. Install-ADDSForest prompts for the DSRM password.

steps.title: 6. RD Gateway, Connection Broker, session hosts, file server
steps.code:
New-RDSessionDeployment -ConnectionBroker rdcb.lab.local -WebAccessServer rdcb.lab.local -SessionHost rdsh1.lab.local
New-RDSessionCollection -CollectionName Desktops -SessionHost rdsh1.lab.local -ConnectionBroker rdcb.lab.local
Add-RDServer -Server rdgw.lab.local -Role RDS-GATEWAY -ConnectionBroker rdcb.lab.local -GatewayExternalFqdn rdgw.example.com
Install-WindowsFeature FS-FileServer -ComputerName fs01.lab.local
Invoke-Command -ComputerName fs01.lab.local { New-Item -ItemType Directory D:\Shares\Data; New-SmbShare -Name Data -Path D:\Shares\Data -ChangeAccess 'LAB\Domain Users' }
steps.note: Install the RD Gateway certificate with its public FQDN (placeholder rdgw.example.com) via Set-RDCertificate.

steps.title: 7. Migrate DC01 to DC02 and move FSMO roles
steps.code:
# On the new server: join the domain, then (only if schema upgrade needed) from the install media
D:\support\adprep\adprep.exe /forestprep
D:\support\adprep\adprep.exe /domainprep
Install-WindowsFeature AD-Domain-Services,DNS -IncludeManagementTools
Install-ADDSDomainController -DomainName lab.local -InstallDns -Credential (Get-Credential LAB\Administrator)
repadmin /replsummary
dcdiag /v
Move-ADDirectoryServerOperationMasterRole -Identity DC02 -OperationMasterRole SchemaMaster,DomainNamingMaster,PDCEmulator,RIDMaster,InfrastructureMaster
netdom query fsmo
steps.note: Point DHCP option 006 and client DNS at DC02, then demote DC01 with Uninstall-ADDSDomainController.

verify: esxcli network vswitch standard list shows vSwitch1 with no uplinks.
From a private VM: ping 8.8.8.8 works; on the gateway, iptables -t nat -L -n -v counts hits.
dcdiag /v and repadmin /replsummary report no errors.
netdom query fsmo lists DC02 for all five roles.
Connect through RD Gateway on 443; Get-RDUserSession lists the session.
pitfalls: vSwitch1 is isolated only until a VM bridges it; the gateway VM is that bridge.
Forgetting ip_forward or the FORWARD rules makes the gateway drop transit traffic silently.
AD breaks when clients use the gateway as DNS; point DHCP at the DC.
Seizing FSMO roles instead of transferring them risks USN rollback if the old DC returns.
Demote DC01 only after replication is clean and DNS and DHCP no longer point at it.
RD Gateway needs a certificate whose name matches the public FQDN.
Thin-provisioned datastores can fill without warning; alert on free space.
keyPoints: ESXi 8.0 runs on bare metal; vSwitch0 uplinks, vSwitch1 stays private.
A dual-NIC gateway VM routes and NATs the private network.
Windows Server 2022 DC provides AD DS, DNS and DHCP.
RD Gateway, Connection Broker and session hosts deliver desktops over HTTPS.
quickDeploy: Install ESXi; set a static management IP.
Create the private vSwitch and gateway VM.
Promote DC01; add RDS roles and file server.
Migrate to DC02: adprep, replicate, move FSMO roles.
osiNote: vSwitch switches frames, gateway NATs, RD Gateway proxies HTTPS.
production: Run two domain controllers; check repadmin /replsummary daily.
Back up VM folders and AD system state before every change.
Disable SSH after use; restrict the sshServer ruleset to the admin subnet.
Set vSwitch security policy to Reject for promiscuous, MAC change and forged transmits.
Watch datastore free space and VM CPU ready time.
